minutes.headline: Capital committee heard the new DPW director's FY22-26 requests, led by a failing public safety chiller; no vote on priorities.
minutes.summary: The DPW director presented his first capital plan request covering facilities, infrastructure and vehicles, drawing on the Vertex building reports. Members questioned the chiller, fire-side space, senior center generator, cemetery ADA work, culverts, grants and a vacuum truck. The committee set its next meeting for prioritization, discussed an open space land-acquisition fund idea, and adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee took no votes and set no priorities; it heard the new DPW director's first capital requests for FY22-26.
The public safety building chiller replacement was listed as the top request, with an estimate from the existing manufacturer that may be a worst case.
Members questioned the chiller, fire-side space, senior center generator, cemetery ADA work, culverts, grants and a stormwater vacuum truck.
The next meeting was set for the 29th to prioritize requests, after a ranking spreadsheet is circulated to members.
An open space land-acquisition fund idea was left for the Finance Committee and Heather to investigate.

why_it_matters: The requests, drawn from building condition reports, are the starting list for capital spending that could reach a town meeting warrant and, for borrowed projects, future tax bills.
The chiller estimate is not firm, and several costs, such as the senior center addition roof, may rise, so final figures could differ from those first presented.
watch_next: The prioritization meeting on the 29th, after the ranking spreadsheet is circulated.
The DPW director's emailed answers to members' questions, and any Finance Committee follow-up on the land-acquisition fund.
